transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks. Well, the main thing that pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. I work as an insurance claims clerk, and even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I just... keep leaving my desk. It's starting to really get in the way of my work, so I figured I needed to talk to someone about it.
Has this difficulty staying at your desk been something you've dealt with since childhood, or is this a new pattern that's developed recently?

Well, looking back, this kind of thing isn't really a brand new pattern for me. I mean, the getting up from my desk all the time is what's causing problems at my job right now, but even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I constantly lost my worksheets. I'd miss instructions, and they always had to give me reminders just to finish my classwork. So, yeah, struggling to just sit and get my work done has definitely been around since I was a kid.
Besides getting up from your desk, do you often feel physically restless or fidgety, or find yourself interrupting others or acting before thinking things through?

Yeah, I definitely get fidgety. Like, if I'm in a training session or one of our longer team meetings at work, I'm usually bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. I just end up shifting around in my chair a lot, even when I'm really trying to look focused on whoever is talking. But as for the other stuff—interrupting people or acting without thinking—I don't really think I do that. It's mostly just the physical restlessness.
Outside of work, do you notice similar restlessness or trouble focusing—like at home, during social activities, or when driving?

Um, I haven't really noticed it much outside of work, to be honest. Like, at home or when I'm just hanging out with friends, I don't really feel that same restlessness. And driving is fine. I think it mostly just stands out at work because I'm supposed to be sitting in one spot looking at claims for eight hours. So, no, I don't really think I have those same issues outside of my job.
Do you notice similar trouble finishing tasks or staying focused when you're doing things at home that require sustained attention, like paying bills, doing chores, or other paperwork?

Um, honestly, not so much with the home stuff. Like I mentioned, it really just seems to hit me at work. But there... yeah, it's a problem. I forget simple work follow-ups way more than I want to admit. Like, I'll completely forget to return a claimant's call, or I'll miss updating a diary note on a file. Or even just... sending a form I meant to send out earlier that day. It just completely slips my mind.

Thinking back to your childhood, did your parents or family also notice you having trouble finishing chores, following instructions, or staying on task at home, or was it something teachers only saw at school?

Um, looking back, this wasn't really a brand new thing for me. I don't remember my parents making a big deal about chores at home, but my teachers definitely noticed it. Like, in elementary school, my teachers used to write comments on my report cards saying that I was bright, but... I was always losing my worksheets. I'd miss instructions a lot, and they constantly had to give me reminders just to finish my classwork.

Do you notice similar trouble staying focused or finishing things when you're doing activities that require sustained concentration outside of work, like reading a book, following a recipe, or working on a personal hobby project?

Not really. Like I said, it's mostly just a work thing for me. If I'm doing something I want to do, like reading or messing around with a hobby, I don't really have an issue staying focused. It's really just when I'm stuck at my desk looking at claims all day that I can't seem to stay on track.
Outside of your job, do you notice yourself forgetting appointments, losing personal items like keys or your phone, or missing deadlines for personal errands and bills?

Um, no, not really. I'm actually pretty good with my personal stuff. I don't really lose my keys or my phone, I just kind of always keep them in my pocket. And for errands or bills... I just use auto-pay or put things in my phone calendar, so I don't really miss those. It really is just... just work where I seem to drop the ball.

Have you had similar jobs or situations in the past—like previous employment or during college—where you had to sit and focus for long periods, and if so, did you notice the same restlessness or trouble finishing tasks there too?

Um, I mean, I went to community college for a couple of years before I got this job, and... I guess I didn't really have the same issues there. I mean, I had to sit through lectures and write papers, but it didn't feel like this. I didn't feel restless or have trouble getting my assignments done. It really just started being a problem when I took this job processing claims.
How do you feel about the actual content of your job—do you find the claims work engaging, or does it feel boring or unfulfilling to you?

Honestly... yeah, it's incredibly boring. It's just the same forms and numbers over and over again all day. There's nothing really engaging about it at all. I mean, it pays the bills, but it's definitely unfulfilling. I just kind of sit there staring at the screen and... yeah, I really don't care about the claims at all.

Have you ever noticed the same restlessness or trouble focusing when you're stuck in other tedious, non-work situations—like sitting through a long, boring lecture, a DMV line, or a lengthy family event?

No, not really. I mean, I guess nobody likes waiting at the DMV, but I don't get that restless, crawling-out-of-my-skin feeling. I just look at my phone or whatever. Even with long family things, I'm fine. It really is just this job.

Thinking back to school, did you have that same trouble focusing and sitting still during subjects or activities you actually found interesting or fun, or was it really just during the boring, repetitive classwork?

Well, thinking about it more... I guess this wasn't completely brand new for me. Even back in elementary school, my teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but... I was always losing my worksheets or missing instructions. They constantly had to remind me to actually finish my classwork. So, I guess I've always kind of struggled with getting things done, even before this job.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's core complaint—restlessness, distractibility, and forgetfulness—is confined almost exclusively to his current job, which he explicitly describes as boring and unfulfilling. He denies similar symptoms in other settings requiring sustained attention (home tasks, bills, hobbies, reading, driving, DMV lines, family events, or even prior schooling/community college), and denies impulsivity or hyperactivity outside work. Although he references childhood teacher comments, these are vague, repetitive, and not corroborated by other cross-setting impairment or parental report, and do not meet the pervasiveness criterion required for ADHD (symptoms must be present in two or more settings). The clinical picture is best explained by a situational, work-specific problem (job dissatisfaction/boredom-related inattention) rather than a neurodevelopmental attention-deficit disorder, supporting a diagnosis of Z56.9 (Problem related to employment, unspecified) rather than ADHD.
